messages.text: Wattimena wins hearts with win vs Littler: 'Beat him, the crowd loves you'

metadata.summary: Jermaine Wattimena was visibly emotional following his massive 10-8 win over Luke Littler in the last 16 at the Grand Slam of Darts, taking in the moment as the Wolverhampton crowd sang his name.
metadata.content: Jermaine Wattimena wins Wolverhampton hearts with victory over Luke Littler: 'You beat him, the crowd loves you' | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Jermaine Wattimena wins Wolverhampton hearts with victory over Luke Littler: 'You beat him, the crowd loves you' Jermaine Wattimena put in a stunning performance to come up with a 10-8 win and dump Luke Littler out of the Grand Slam in the second round; you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports until November 22 Wednesday 18 November 2026 23:16, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the second-round match between Luke Littler and Jermaine Wattimena at the Grand Slam of Darts Jermaine Wattimena was visibly emotional following his massive 10-8 win over Luke Littler in the last 16 at the Grand Slam of Darts, taking in the moment as the Wolverhampton crowd sang his name. An English crowd chanting so heartily for a Dutch player is somewhat of a rarity, especially when they are taking on an Englishman, but it was the sensational manner of his victory over the world No 1 and back-to-back Grand Slam champion that won them over. Littler was aiming for a Grand Slam three-peat after his wins in 2024 and 2025 but with the Dutchman prevailing, it is still only Phil Taylor and Michael van Gerwen who have achieved such a feat. messages.text: Cadillac confirm Bottas to stay with team for 2027

metadata.summary: Cadillac have confirmed Valtteri Bottas will stay on at the team for the 2027 Formula 1 season, ending speculation about the Finnish driver's future.
metadata.content: Valtteri Bottas: Cadillac confirm Finnish driver to stay with team for 2027 Formula 1 season ahead of Las Vegas Grand Prix | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Valtteri Bottas: Cadillac confirm Finnish driver to stay with team for 2027 Formula 1 season ahead of Las Vegas Grand Prix Valtteri Bottas will remain with Cadillac next year after speculation his future at the team was in doubt; watch the Las Vegas GP weekend on Sky Sports F1, with Friday's practice sessions at 12.30am and 4pm By Nigel Chiu in Las Vegas Wednesday 18 November 2026 20:14, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking at the Sao Paulo GP, Valtteri Bottas said 'nothing has changed' and he was hopeful of staying with Cadillac for the long term Cadillac have confirmed Valtteri Bottas will stay on at the team for the 2027 Formula 1 season, ending speculation about the Finnish driver's future. Bottas returned after a year's absence from the grid for this season, Cadillac's first in the sport, as one of two hugely experienced drivers for the all-new American team's first line-up alongside Sergio Perez, who signed a contract extension last month until at least 2029. But, Bottas' future has been up in the air recently as Cadillac pushed for American Formula 2 driver Colton Herta to earn a Formula 1 super licence, which he secured two weeks ago, by running him in practice sessions. messages.text: Sober Glory storms to victory over Old Park Star on chase debut

metadata.summary: Sober Glory turned the tables on Supreme Novices’ Hurdle conqueror Old Park Star to make a faultless chasing bow in the Golwg Gwendraeth Beginners’ Chase at Ffos Las.
metadata.content: Sober Glory storms to victory over Old Park Star on chase debut | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Sober Glory storms to victory over Old Park Star on chase debut A dramatic afternoon at Ffos Las saw Sober Glory soar to success on chase debut for the Hobbs and White team with old rival Old Park Star fading into third with a broken blood vessel. Wednesday 18 November 2026 15:37, UK Image: Sober Glory ridden by Harry Cobden wins the William Hill Racing Epic Boosts Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race) at Newbury Racecourse Sober Glory turned the tables on Supreme Novices’ Hurdle conqueror Old Park Star to make a faultless chasing bow in the Golwg Gwendraeth Beginners’ Chase at Ffos Las. One of the most eagerly-anticipated showdowns of the early season as the dry spell forced the exciting duo to west Wales, the main protagonists were immediately to the fore with Philip Hobbs and Johnson White's Sober Glory the more sure-footed of the duo in the early exchanges. There was little to separate the pair as a fine leap four out brought the Nico de Boinville-ridden Old Park Star alongside, but Ben Jones soon reclaimed the advantage in the home straight aboard the 5-4 second favourite. With the gap growing all the way up the home straight, the Cheltenham Festival runner-up gained revenge over Nicky Henderson's 4-5 favourite, sauntering to an impressive nine-and-a-half length opening victory over fences. messages.text: Banned Springboks coach Erasmus invites fans to watch along of Ireland game

metadata.summary: Rassie Erasmus has invited fans to join a live watch-along online of South Africa's clash against Ireland, after the Springboks coach was suspended for six matches for comments he made about match officials.
metadata.content: Rassie Erasmus: South Africa coach invites fans to watch-along of Springboks clash vs Ireland following six-match ban | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Rassie Erasmus: South Africa coach invites fans to watch-along of Springboks clash vs Ireland following six-match ban Springboks coach Rassie Erasmus was handed a six-match suspension for comments he made about referees following South Africa's Nations Championship defeat by France; South Africa Rugby have requested a full hearing into his ban Wednesday 18 November 2026 17:44, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rassie Erasmus is inviting members of the public to join a live 'watch-along' of South Africa's game against Ireland Rassie Erasmus has invited fans to join a live watch-along online of South Africa's clash against Ireland, after the Springboks coach was suspended for six matches for comments he made about match officials. Erasmus had questioned whether there were double standards in the officiating of South Africa's 21-19 defeat to France during a press conference earlier in the week, prompting an investigation from World Rugby , who later said that the coach had "disrespected the authority of the officials".
